mechanism: Chronic WGD/CIN represses cGAS–STING signaling, driving an immunosuppressive TIME
readouts: WGD score; aneuploidy metrics; STING1 expression; IFN/immune signatures; myeloid-inflamed TIME
control_levers: CIN-aware IO strategies; consider STING agonists where reversible; adjust IO intensity to CIN burden
notes: Biphasic with acute DDR—requires explicit context tagging.

mechanism: Acute DNA damage generates cytosolic DNA, activating cGAS–STING and type I IFN, priming IO
readouts: pSTING; pIRF3; type I IFN signatures; acute DDR markers
control_levers: Schedule PARP/ATR/CHK1 with ICI to capture STING/IFN burst while managing toxicity
notes: Opposes chronic WGD/CIN effect; edge must be tagged as acute.

mechanism: Telomere crisis generates dicentrics and breakage–fusion–bridge cycles, causing aneuploidy and chromothripsis
context: ALT or telomerase insufficiency; telomere crisis
readouts: Telomere fusions; dicentric chromosomes; telomere length; ALT markers
control_levers: Monitor telomere status; explore telomerase/ALT-directed strategies when translationally ready
notes: Key Seed→Switch edge; locks telomere biology into CIN/WGD.

mechanism: ecDNA amplicons create high transcriptional output and replication–transcription conflicts, generating RS and CHK1 dependency
readouts: ecDNA by WGS/FISH; AmpliconArchitect/circle-seq; RS gene signatures; γH2AX; pCHK1
control_levers: Combine ecDNA payload inhibitors with CHK1/ATR; deploy replication-conflict targeting agents (e.g., BBI-2779-class)
notes: Translational Nature/NCI data support ecDNA-linked RS/CHK1 vulnerability.

mechanism: Lactate and adenosine accumulation in hypoxic, glycolytic tumors suppress effector cells and favor myeloid/Treg programs
context: hypoxia; high glycolysis; acidic and adenosine-rich niche
readouts: MCT1/4 expression; extracellular pH; A2A axis markers; hypoxia signatures
control_levers: Vessel/chemistry normalization; A2A antagonists; lactate/MCT-directed strategies combined with IO
notes: Core immunometabolic bottleneck with multiple drugs in or near clinical testing.

mechanism: LOX-driven ECM crosslinking and stiffness activate YAP/TAZ and abnormal vessels, promoting EMT, intravasation, and resistance
context: desmoplastic, stiff stroma; high LOX/YAP–TAZ activity
readouts: LOX activity; stiffness metrics (e.g., elastography); YAP/TAZ target gene expression; vessel maturity indices
control_levers: LOX/FAK/YAP–TAZ inhibitors; vessel normalization; stromal-modulating agents
notes: Mechanobiology overlay edge; connects Sink to Spread and resistance.

mechanism: Exosomal ncRNA cargo and integrin profiles condition organ-specific pre-metastatic niches

control_levers: Block EV release/uptake (emerging agents); target downstream PMN effectors; monitor EV signatures for metastatic trajectory
notes: Based on exosomal integrin organotropism; interventions still early-stage.

mechanism: Epi-plasticity generates drug-tolerant persister states and therapy-induced lineage switches that seed genetic resistance

control_levers: Short-course epi add-ons (EZH2/HDAC/CDK7/9) around targeted agents; adaptive dosing; re-differentiation strategies
notes: Reversible DTP states are well documented; regimen optimization ongoing.

mechanism: CHIP and aging drive SASP and immunosenescence, biasing toward a permissive, inflamed but ineffective TIME and confounding ctDNA

control_levers: Anti-inflammatory strategies; senolytics in trials; mandatory WBC sequencing to de-CHIP ctDNA
notes: Strong epidemiology and mechanism; definitive interventional trials ongoing.

mechanism: Post-therapy resistant clones, often CIN/ecDNA-high, reseed the mutational landscape and drive further evolution

control_levers: Evolution-aware combination/sequencing strategies that close bypass routes; adaptive therapy guided by clonal tracking
notes: Operationally closes the MVCL; central to adaptive trial design.

control_levers: Plasticity-state targeting; lineage-state suppression; combination timing; resistance-window monitoring
